text: Lump-free curd is pumped into moulds and knits together mainly under its own weight while kept warm (around 41 °C). This light pressing leaves the many small, irregular, rice-grain-sized eyes and a soft but sliceable texture with a mild, acidic taste.

steps.note: The curd is pumped into moulds, kept at about 41 °C, and pressed very lightly or not at all.
The rind of the rinded type is formed by smear bacteria; the rindless type is ripened 3 weeks at 12–20 °C under film.
